record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures Associated with the Invariant Subspace Problem
record.original_question: For which bounded operators T on a separable real or complex Banach space X does there exist a non-trivial closed T-invariant subspace M, meaning a closed subspace M with M not equal to {0} and M not equal to X such that T(M) is contained in M?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional separable Banach space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator. A closed subspace $M \subseteq X$ is called $T$-invariant if $T(M) \subseteq M$, and it is called non-trivial if $M \neq \{0\}$ and $M \neq X$. Characterize the bounded linear operators $T$ on $X$ for which there exists a non-trivial closed $T$-invariant subspace. In particular, determine whether every bounded linear operator on a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space admits a non-trivial closed invariant subspace.
artifact.status_search_result: The invariant subspace problem is solved negatively in the general Banach space setting: Enflo (1987) and Read (1984) constructed bounded operators on separable Banach spaces with no non-trivial closed invariant subspace, and Read later gave such examples on $\ell^1$. The Hilbert space version remains a famous open problem. Recent preprints (e.g., Enflo 2023 and Neville) claiming resolutions in the Hilbert case have not been accepted as verified by the community as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Invariant subspace problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: For Banach spaces Enflo and Read produced counterexamples; for separable Hilbert spaces the problem remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Solved negatively for general Banach spaces, still open for separable Hilbert spaces.
